mnemonic: The heart 忄 has hold of something it will not put down, and standing in this spot brings the whole lot back up. This place, for me: なつかしい.
notes: English has no clean word for it. Not sad and not merely fond, more that the past has come close enough to touch.
sentence: ここは私にとって懐かしい場所です。
sentence_meaning: This is a nostalgic place for me.

mnemonic: Not likely and you know it perfectly well, and you are going to say it out loud regardless. If she ever said yes: もしも.
notes: もし is the plain if. もしも is the same word held a beat longer, and it leans on how unlikely the thing is.
sentence: もしも彼女と結婚できたらどんなに嬉しいだろう。
sentence_meaning: If I could ever marry her, how happy I would be!

mnemonic: What was in you from the start 才 crossed with what you can actually do 能. He is full of the artistic sort: さいのう.
notes: 能力 のうりょく is ability you built up. 才能 is the part you were born holding.
sentence: 彼は芸術的な才能にあふれているね。
sentence_meaning: He is full of artistic talent.

meaning: to make a break for, to run off
mnemonic: You get away 逃 and then you are out 出 and still moving, which is two stages rather than one. The tiger is not in the cage: にげだす.
sentence: トラがおりから逃げ出しました。
sentence_meaning: The tiger escaped from the cage.

mnemonic: One sort 様 and then the mark that says do that again 々, and the city has the whole range of them in it: さまざま.
notes: 色々 いろいろ is the everyday various. 様々 is a shade more formal and sits better in writing.
sentence: その都市には様々な人種が集まっているわ。
sentence_meaning: There are diverse ethnic groups in that city.

mnemonic: The place 院 you end up at once the sickness 疒 has wrapped itself properly round you. Off we go: びょういん.
sentence: 病院へ行きます。
sentence_meaning: I will go to the hospital.

mnemonic: Two figures stood side by side and facing the same way so that the difference shows up. Set against Japan, my country is freezing: くらべる.
sentence: 日本と比べると、私の国はとても寒いです。
sentence_meaning: Compared to Japan, my country is very cold.

mnemonic: The same stuff that came out of the tap, gone hard enough to knock against the side of the glass. In mine, please: こおり.
sentence: グラスに氷を入れてください。
sentence_meaning: Please put some ice in my glass.

mnemonic: An animal 犭 held between 夾 two walls with nowhere at all to turn round. My room is very much like that: せまい.
notes: 細い ほそい is thin as in a thread or a finger. 狭い is narrow as in not enough room, and 広い ひろい is its opposite.
sentence: 私の部屋は狭いです。
sentence_meaning: My room is cramped.

mnemonic: The god 神 with the highest honorific 様 on the end, which is how you address one rather than how you describe one. I asked for something: かみさま.
notes: 神 かみ on its own is a god, and Shinto has a great many of them. 神様 is the one you actually speak to.
sentence: 神様にお願いしました。
sentence_meaning: I asked a favor to God.

mnemonic: Moving 動 and swaying 揺 at once, and it is not the building doing it. She heard the news and could not hold still: どうよう.
sentence: 彼女はその知らせを聞いて激しく動揺した。
sentence_meaning: She trembled violently upon hearing that news.

mnemonic: The one with the long hair in the old drawing, which meant the eldest and so the one in charge. That monkey runs the group: ちょう.
notes: 頭 あたま is the head on your shoulders. 長 is the head of a group, and it goes on the end of a title: 社長, 部長.
sentence: あの大きなサルは群れの長だ。
sentence_meaning: That big monkey is the leader of the group.

mnemonic: The main business is finished and there is one more thing that has to be said before anybody leaves. If it rains, it is off: なお.
notes: Formal, and it turns up at the foot of notices. それに and 他に add a point in speech.
sentence: なお、雨の場合は中止です。
sentence_meaning: Moreover, it will be canceled in the event of rain.

mnemonic: Things 物 told 語 one after another until between them they add up to something. Adventures, mostly: ものがたり.
notes: 話 はなし is a talk or a story in the everyday sense. 物語 is a tale, the sort that gets written down.
sentence: 私は冒険の物語が大好きです。
sentence_meaning: I love adventure stories.

mnemonic: A phrase 句 of writing 文 that somebody has clearly been rehearsing, and she has one ready every single time: もんく.
notes: 文句を言う is to complain. On its own 文句 can also simply mean the wording of something.
sentence: 彼女はいつも文句ばかり言う。
sentence_meaning: She always does nothing but complain.

mnemonic: The arrow comes down and lands and the flight is over. We got to a conclusion in the end: いたる.
sentence: ようやく結論に至ったようね。
sentence_meaning: It seemed that we finally reached a conclusion.

mnemonic: Ten minutes over the flame and turn it once, and the entire house knows what is for dinner: さかな.
sentence: 魚を10分くらい焼きます。
sentence_meaning: I will cook the fish for about 10 minutes.

mnemonic: Up off the fence and away before you have the camera out of your pocket. There goes one: とり.
sentence: 鳥が飛んでいます。
sentence_meaning: A bird is flying.

mnemonic: Light 日 lands in the middle 央 of the glass and something that is not in the room appears in it. A man's shadow, in the window: うつる.
notes: 現れる あらわれる is a thing actually turning up. 映る is an image of it landing on a surface, and it is the word for showing on a screen.
sentence: 窓に男性の影が映っています。
sentence_meaning: The shadow of a man is reflected in the window.

mnemonic: One 一 life 生, the whole of it end to end, which is how large the favour is being made out to be: いっしょう.
sentence: 一生のお願いがあります。
sentence_meaning: I have a once-in-a-lifetime favor to ask.

mnemonic: Thread mashed flat and dried out, and the present goes inside it. Pick a nice one: かみ.
notes: Three かみ in this deck: 紙 paper, 髪 hair and 神 a god. The characters are the only thing keeping them apart.
sentence: プレゼントをきれいな紙で包みました。
sentence_meaning: I wrapped the present in beautiful paper.

meaning: to be called..., to speak (humble form)
mnemonic: You give your own name and lower yourself in the act of giving it, which is the whole point of the verb. Suzuki, if you please: もうす.
notes: The humble form of 言う. Used about yourself and never about anybody else, exactly like 致す いたす.
sentence: 私は鈴木と申します。
sentence_meaning: My name is Suzuki.

mnemonic: Layer 複 on layer with everything mixed through it 雑 and none of it sorted. That program is a mess: ふくざつ.
notes: 単純 たんじゅん is the direct contrast, simple as in uncomplicated, and 簡単 かんたん is simple as in easy.
sentence: このプログラムはとても複雑です。
sentence_meaning: This program is very complicated.

mnemonic: The hand lets go halfway through the swing and the thing carries on without it. Over here, please: なげる.
sentence: ボールをこっちに投げてください。
sentence_meaning: Please throw the ball over here.

mnemonic: A thing 事 that came about 出来 rather than one anybody arranged. Something interesting happened: できごと.
notes: 発生 はっせい is the formal one, for accidents and incidents. 出来事 is an everyday occurrence, good or bad.
sentence: 面白い出来事がありました。
sentence_meaning: Something interesting happened.

mnemonic: The part of the department 部 that sits under 下 you, and his are rather good at their jobs: ぶか.
sentence: 彼は優秀な部下を持っているわね。
sentence_meaning: He has outstanding subordinates, doesn't he?

mnemonic: Not merely enough but visibly more than enough, and the dish is heavy in the hand with it: たっぷり.
sentence: この料理は、栄養がたっぷりですよ。
sentence_meaning: This dish contains plenty of nutrition.

mnemonic: The power 力 you actually 実 have rather than the one printed on the certificate. The two of them are level: じつりょく.
sentence: 二人の実力は互角です。
sentence_meaning: Their abilities are evenly matched.

mnemonic: Left 左 and right 右 in the one word and in that order, which is the reverse of the English. Both ways before you cross: さゆう.
sentence: 通りを渡る前に左右を見た。
sentence_meaning: I looked left and right before crossing the street.

mnemonic: Two characters for choosing stacked up, one walking the row 選 and one measuring by hand 択. Five to pick from: せんたく.
sentence: この5種類から選択できます。
sentence_meaning: You can select one from these five types.

mnemonic: You go round the thing 調 and then through it a layer at a time 査. We are looking into that one: ちょうさ.
sentence: 私たちがその問題を調査しています。
sentence_meaning: We're investigating that problem.

mnemonic: You pull one person 亻 out of the row 列 to show everybody what you mean. This software, say: たとえば.
sentence: 例えば、このソフトで日本語を勉強することができます。
sentence_meaning: For example, you could use this software to study Japanese.

mnemonic: You watch 見 and you send 送 and then you stand there on the concourse while the plane goes. He was off abroad: みおくる.
sentence: 彼が外国に行くのを見送りました。
sentence_meaning: I saw him off on his trip overseas.

mnemonic: Nothing he said was unreasonable and there is no part of it you can argue with, which is its own sort of annoying: もっとも.
notes: Same reading as 最も もっとも, the most, which is written with the character. This one stays in kana and means fair enough.
sentence: 彼の意見はもっともです。
sentence_meaning: His opinion is quite right.

mnemonic: You walk along behind whoever is in front and do not strike out on your own. She did not: したがう.
sentence: 彼女は命令に従わなかった。
sentence_meaning: She did not obey orders.

meaning: to let pass, to run through
mnemonic: You make the thing go the whole way through 通 rather than standing there watching it. Thread, through a needle: とおす.
notes: 通る とおる is a thing passing through by itself. 通す is you putting it through.
sentence: 針に糸を通してください。
sentence_meaning: Please thread the needle.

mnemonic: You take the gap 間 the wrong way round 違 and land on the wrong answer. On an easy one, at that: まちがえる.
notes: 間違う まちがう is being wrong. 間違える is getting a particular thing wrong, or taking one thing for another.
sentence: やさしい問題を間違えてしまいました。
sentence_meaning: I made a mistake on an easy question.

mnemonic: Power 力 that the body 体 has rather than the arms, which is what lets somebody go all day. The young have it: たいりょく.
sentence: 若者は体力がありますね。
sentence_meaning: Young people have a lot of stamina.

meaning: to accomplish, to carry out, to fulfill
mnemonic: The tree puts out its fruit 果 in the end, and you do the thing you said you were going to. He got it done: はたす.
sentence: 彼はしっかりと責任を果たしました。
sentence_meaning: He fulfilled his responsibilities diligently.

meaning: to make a racket, to mess around
mnemonic: A horse 馬 with something biting at it, in a carriage, at eight in the morning. Not in here, thank you: さわぐ.
notes: ふざける is messing about. 騒ぐ is the noise that messing about makes.
sentence: 電車の中で騒がないでください。
sentence_meaning: Please don't make a racket in the train.

mnemonic: Off the edge 飛 and straight in 込 without stopping to test the water. The frog did not think twice: とびこむ.
sentence: カエルが池に飛び込んだね。
sentence_meaning: The frog jumped into the pond.

meaning: to increase, to augment, to rise
mnemonic: Earth 土 going onto the heap and the heap getting taller, and the river has been at it all week: ます.
notes: 増える ふえる is a thing increasing by itself and 増やす ふやす is you increasing it. 増す does both and is the more formal word.
sentence: 大雨で川の水かさが増しているな。
sentence_meaning: The amount of water in the river rose due to heavy rains.

mnemonic: Metal on concrete and the sound of it carrying a street away. The car found the pole: ぶつかる.
sentence: 車が電柱にぶつかった。
sentence_meaning: The car crashed into the telephone pole.

mnemonic: A thought 思 that comes back out 出 on its own years afterwards. The trip left you a few: おもいで.
notes: 記憶 きおく is memory as the faculty. 思い出 is one particular memory that you keep.
sentence: 旅行で楽しい思い出ができました。
sentence_meaning: I made fun memories during my trip.

mnemonic: The heaven 天 of the room, with a frame of beams 井 laid across it. This one is a long way up: てんじょう.
sentence: この部屋は天井が高いですね。
sentence_meaning: This room has a high ceiling.

mnemonic: The one carrying the axe 兵 and serving 士 rather than choosing. Three of them hurt in the bombing: へいし.
sentence: その爆撃で兵士が３人負傷しました。
sentence_meaning: Three soldiers were injured in that bombing.

mnemonic: Filled 満 right to the edge with nothing at all left to add. The moon got there last night: みちる.
notes: 満たす みたす is you filling something. 満ちる is it filling up on its own.
sentence: 月が満ちてきましたね。
sentence_meaning: The moon has become full, hasn't it?

meaning: can't stand, can't put up with
mnemonic: Past the point where you can sit with it and get on with anything else at all. Your head, this afternoon: たまらない.
notes: Also used of good things: 美味しくてたまらない is so good you cannot bear it.
sentence: 頭が痛くてたまらない。
sentence_meaning: I have an unbearable headache.

mnemonic: You take the taste 味 slowly instead of swallowing, because it is your mother's cooking and you have not had it in a year: あじわう.
sentence: 母の手料理をゆっくり味わいました。
sentence_meaning: I took my time savoring my mother's cooking.

mnemonic: Out 出 through the door with somewhere to be, which is a good deal more than stepping outside. Sundays, mostly: でかける.
notes: 出る でる is going out of a place or coming out of one. 出かける is setting off somewhere with an errand attached, and 消える きえる is the other go out, a light or a flame.
sentence: 日曜日によく出かけます。
sentence_meaning: I often go out on Sundays.
